observations: Photo 0 shows a V-configuration car engine with "PORSCHE" embossed on both sides of the valve cover, surrounded by other engines in a yard setting.
Photo 1 shows the same or a similar engine from the side, with alternator, serpentine belt, intake hoses, and throttle body visible.
Photo 2 shows an engine with what appears to be a transmission or gearbox attached on the right side, plus alternator, belts, and ancillaries.
All three photos carry the watermark "EZE PORSCHE GLOBAL AUTOS".
No engine block casting number, emissions sticker, or specific model code is legible in any photo.

claims.claim: We also deals on all kinds of car spare parts
claims.evidence: Seller's text only; photos show engines but cannot verify the scope of the seller's business.

risks.risk: Engine does not run or is seized internally
risks.proof: Video of the crankshaft turning by hand or with the starter, or a compression test

risks.risk: Specific Porsche engine model unknown, which sets the value
risks.proof: Clear photo of the engine block casting number or emissions sticker with the engine code

risks.risk: Internal damage such as cracked block or worn bearings not visible externally
risks.proof: Borescope inspection photos of the cylinders or a teardown inspection

risks.risk: Missing ancillaries such as ECU, sensors, or wiring harness
risks.proof: Itemized photo or video showing every part included with the engine

proof_requests: Clear photo of the engine block casting number or model code sticker
Video of the engine cranking or turning over
Photo showing whether a transmission or gearbox is attached
Itemized photo or list of all included sensors, harness, and ECU
response.reason: The photos show a Porsche car engine, but the specific model or engine code that determines its value is unreadable, so even a worst-case price cannot be set without that proof.
